creator: UT Austin / Bob Harms

role: Herbarium voucher / thickened rootstock and crown context
creator: UT Plant Resources Center / University of Texas Herbarium
source_context: Look at the central and lower-left mounted plants, where several stems meet a thickened crown and a taproot extends below it. The voucher supplies crown/rootstock context with the original ruler retained; it does not establish living color, plant age or internal wood anatomy.

role: Capsule and leaf close-up / smooth fruit and rounded entire leaves
creator: Eric Keith
source_context: Look at the smooth green capsule above the cyathium and the small opposite rounded leaves. Narrow appendages at some nodes provide context but do not securely demonstrate the complete linear-stipule architecture. Rootstock and seed are absent.

role: Extracted pale seed and opened capsule / surface and form reference
creator: Andrey Zharkikh
source_context: Look at the isolated pale seed at upper right beside the opened green capsule pieces. Its form and low surface relief are visible. Physiological maturity and grid units are not established by this photo, so do not use it to certify mature seed color or size.

role: Stipule macro / narrow paired stipules with upper branches
creator: UT Austin / Bob Harms
source_context: Find the pale narrow stipules rising close together at the leaf bases. Their upper portions have hairlike branches. Compare these with the broad fused scale in E. serpens; closeness alone does not demonstrate fusion. The original 1 mm scale bar is retained.

role: Seed macro / multiple faces and calibrated scale
creator: Nathan Taylor
source_context: Compare the four pale seeds on the dark background: different faces reveal the angular form and low surface relief. The author specifies 0.5 mm scale divisions. Fine surface texture is visible at this magnification; do not confuse it with the strong transverse ridges of E. prostrata. Physiological maturity is not explicitly documented.

role: Seed face macro / angular outline and low surface relief
creator: Nathan Taylor
source_context: Look at the pale seed above the scale: its angular outline and face texture are visible. The observation author specifies 0.5 mm scale divisions. This complementary angle belongs to the same identified seed series; physiological maturity is not explicitly documented.
